translations.source_sense_description: просыпавшись, оказаться разбросанным, лежащим в виде мелких частей

glosses: To drop something so that it spreads out or makes a mess; to accidentally pour.

examples.text: I spilled some sticky juice on the kitchen floor.

glosses: To spread out or fall out, as above.

examples.text: Some sticky juice spilled onto the kitchen floor.
He was so topful of himself, that he let it spill on all the company.

glosses: To overflow out of a designated area.

examples.text: The crowd spilled onto Maple Avenue.

glosses: To drop something that was intended to be caught.

examples.text: That should have been that, but Hart caught a dose of the Hennessey wobbles and spilled Adlene Guedioura's long-range shot.

glosses: To mar; to damage; to destroy by misuse; to waste.

examples.text: They [the colours] disfigure the stuff and spill the whole workmanship.
Spill not the morning (the quintessence of day) in recreations.

glosses: To be destroyed, ruined, or wasted; to come to ruin; to perish; to waste.

examples.text: That thou wilt suffer innocence to spill.
This winter’s weather it waxeth cold, / And frost it freezeth on every hill, / And Boreas blows his blast so bold / That all our cattle are like to spill.

glosses: To overflow or flow out, over or off something.

examples.text: Liverpool Street's 1985-92 remodelling by the British Rail Architects' Department (under project lead Nick Derbyshire) had carefully followed original 1870s detailing, with the concourse designed to allow natural light to spill into the station.

glosses: To cause or flow out and be lost or wasted; to shed.

examples.text: to revenge his Blood, ſo juſtly ſpilt, / VVhat is it leſs then to partake his guilt?

glosses: To cause to be thrown from a mount, a carriage, etc.

examples.text: Then, not thirty feet beyond, a sudden panicky lunge to the side by his horse spilled him from the saddle.

glosses: To cover or decorate with slender pieces of wood, metal, ivory, etc.; to inlay.

examples.text: And all the others pavement were with yvory spilt

glosses: To relieve a sail from the pressure of the wind, so that it can be more easily reefed or furled, or to lessen the strain.
To open the leadership of a parliamentary party for re-election.
To reveal information to an uninformed party.

examples.text: He spilled his guts out to his new psychologist.
‘You wanted to know where we were going. Follow me. I’m going to spill it.’

glosses: To come undone.
To express (something), especially repeatedly or floridly; to be expressed.

examples.text: He spilled insults about the other team.
Praise spilled from him every day.

glosses: A mess of something that has been dropped.
A fall or stumble.

examples.text: The bruise is from a bad spill he had last week.

glosses: A small stick or piece of paper used to light a candle, cigarette etc by the transfer of a flame from a fire.

examples.text: “In a moment, he has torn the letter into long thin strips, and rolling them up into spills he thrusts them hurriedly in amongst the other spills in the vase on the mantle-piece.”
Kit froze with the pipe between his teeth, the relit spill pressed to the weed within it.

glosses: A slender piece of anything.
A peg or pin for plugging a hole, as in a cask'; a spile.
A slender piece of anything.
A metallic rod or pin.
A slender piece of anything.
A spillikin.

examples.text: A tool with which to extract the spills from the pile.

glosses: A slender piece of anything.
A splinter caught in the skin.
One of the thick laths or poles driven horizontally ahead of the main timbering in advancing a level in loose ground.
The situation where sound is picked up by a microphone from a source other than that which is intended.
A small sum of money.

examples.text: Spill or Sportule for the same from the credulous Laity

glosses: A declaration that the leadership of a parliamentary party is vacant, and open for re-election. Short form of leadership spill.

translations.source_sense_description: просыпавшись, оказаться разбросанным, лежащим в виде мелких частей

glosses: To (cause to) separate and go in different directions; to disperse.

examples.text: The crowd scattered in terror.
Scatter and disperse the giddy Goths.

glosses: To distribute loosely as by sprinkling.

examples.text: Her ashes were scattered at the top of a waterfall.
Why should my muse enlarge on Libyan swains, / Their scattered cottages, and ample plains?

glosses: To deflect (radiation or particles).

examples.text: Chasca's ring is unique. It appears to be, for lack of a better term, a massive piece of alien "installation art." The rings are made of small pieces of synthetic material, and are almost invisible from space. From the ground, they catch and scatter the light of Matano in picturesque ways. It is not known who created the ring or when.

glosses: To occur or fall at widely spaced intervals.
To frustrate, disappoint, and overthrow.

examples.text: to scatter hopes or plans

glosses: To be dispersed upon.

examples.text: Desiccated stalks scattered the fields.
[…] its beauty is obscured by the environmental waste and loose trash that scatter the countryside.

glosses: Of a pitcher: to keep down the number of hits or walks.
To leave.

examples.text: When the police showed up, I scattered.

glosses: The act of scattering or dispersing.
A collection of dispersed objects.

examples.text: The Los Angeles Basin evolved as a mobility surface principally through the combination of an initial system of electric railways connecting a scatter of agricultural settlement settlements.

A broad scatter of kurgan graves in the steppes contained imported Tripolye C2 pots (among other imported pot types) and a few, like Serezlievka, also contained Tripolye-like schematic rod-headed figurines.
The plot of all our sea-level index points shows a scatter of data points that do not overlap […]
